propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Deus, qui nobis, in Corde Filii tui, nostris vulnerato peccatis,
infinitos dilectionis thesauros misericorditer largiri dignaris:
concede, quaesumus; ut, illi devotum pietatis nostrae praestantes
obsequium, dignae quoque satisfactionis exhibeamus officium. Per
eundem Dominum.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 3 tokens differ only in accent, ligature or orthography as the 1862 text layer renders them (D6mine/Domine; quo/quo,; vivis,/vivis); 1862 text layer reads 'Eteebeant' where the 1962 prints 'Praebeant'; 1862 text layer reads 'tervorem' where the 1962 prints 'fervorem:'; 1862 text layer reads 'suavit' where the 1962 prints 'suavitate'; 1862 text layer reads 'perc6pta,' where the 1962 prints 'percepta;'; 1862 text layer reads 'disc' where the 1962 prints 'discamus'; 1862 text layer reads 'terr6na' where the 1962 prints 'terrena'; 1862 text layer reads 'aespicere,' where the 1962 prints 'despicere,'; 1862 text layer reads 're' where the 1962 prints 'amare'; 1862 text layer reads 'ccel6stia.' where the 1962 prints 'caelestia:'; 1862 text layer emits 3 stray fragment(s) at line breaks ('te', 'mus', 'am'); 1962 writes the conclusion out at length (cum Deo Patre in unitate.); the 1862 prints the shorter cue. Corroboration: 1922 Tours Mame, printed p. 921 (artifact PDF p. 1035), text layer, lines 81737-81747: 22 of 22 tokens match exactly or in orthography, 0 word-level difference(s).
